title: Residue fibers and character Fourier coordinates
pvg_object: valuation points projected through labeled primes to units modulo q
forward_translation: Reduced residue indicators decompose into character coordinates with explicit principal mode.
reverse_translation: All character coefficients recover a function on the reduced residue group; aggregated energies do not.
preserved_information: full finite Fourier data when phases and labels are retained
lost_information: unlabeled exponent multisets do not determine residues; moment aggregation loses phase
trigger: The problem restricts n to a reduced residue class or compares residue fibers.
error_or_wall: Prime labels modulo q are essential; pure exponent geometry is insufficient.
required_certificate: Fix normalization, treat primes dividing q, and distinguish full coefficients from moments.
positive_example: Modulo 5, the four character coordinates recover any function on the four reduced classes.
counterexample: Two integers with the same exponent multiset can lie in different residue classes.
anti_overclaim: Character decomposition is exact but supplies no cancellation by itself.
classification: Known exact Fourier bridge / label-dependence warning

title: Principal-mode removal and balanced residue fluctuations
pvg_object: subtracting the average fiber mass before comparing residue geometry
forward_translation: Centering residue-fiber data deletes the constant Fourier mode and isolates nonprincipal characters.
reverse_translation: Adding back the mean restores the full fiber function if the centered data are retained.
preserved_information: all nonprincipal fluctuations and their phases
lost_information: the total mean is lost unless stored separately
trigger: The question concerns bias, variance, or equidistribution around a main term.
typical_output: balanced sums with zero total fiber mass
error_or_wall: Failure to remove the principal mode confounds mean size with distributional fluctuation.
required_certificate: Record the exact mean and normalization before subtracting it.
positive_example: Centering [1,3,5,7] by its mean 4 gives a vector summing to zero.
counterexample: A small centered variance does not recover the omitted mean.
anti_overclaim: Principal subtraction is normalization, not evidence of equidistribution.

title: Residue-fiber variance and character second moments
pvg_object: L2 energy of centered mass across residue fibers
ant_object: sum of squared nonprincipal character coefficients via Parseval
forward_translation: Parseval converts centered fiber variance into a normalized nonprincipal character second moment.
reverse_translation: Second moments recover total energy but not individual phases or character identities.
lost_information: phase, sign, localization, higher moments, and individual exceptional characters
trigger: The observable compares variance across reduced residue classes.
error_or_wall: An L2 bound does not imply a uniform pointwise bound for every residue class.
required_certificate: State Fourier normalization and any passage from average to maximum.
positive_example: A four-point centered vector and its discrete Fourier transform have equal normalized energy.
counterexample: Two Fourier spectra can have the same energy and different phases.
anti_overclaim: Second-moment control is not pointwise equidistribution.
classification: Known exact energy bridge / phase-loss audit
